countries.overview: German politics is dominated by Chancellor Friedrich Merz's nomination of CSU politician Ilse Aigner as candidate for the federal presidency, paving the way for the country's first female head of state. As Germany marks November 9 with calls to defend democratic values, a new survey highlights public dissatisfaction with the functioning of democracy, while political tensions simmer over a proposed plastics tax. Additional domestic focus centers on a security breach involving a flag replacement at the Reichstag, the struggling FDP's party conference, and delays in releasing federal funds for educational infrastructure.

items.title: Chancellor Merz Nominates Ilse Aigner for Federal President
items.summary: After weeks of deliberation, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced his support for CSU politician Ilse Aigner to become the next federal president. Both plan to appear together before the press to make the nomination official. If elected, Aigner would be the first woman to hold the post.

items.title: November 9 Commemorations and Concerns Over Democracy
items.summary: Marking the historic date of November 9, commissioner Evelyn Zupke warned against political misrepresentation of the peaceful revolution in East Germany, while Chancellor Merz called for defending democracy. The commemorations coincide with a new ARD poll showing that only one in three Germans believes democracy currently functions well in the country.

items.title: Union Parliamentary Leader Rejects Planned Plastics Tax
items.summary: Thorsten Frei, parliamentary leader of the CDU/CSU conservative bloc, has rejected plans for a national plastics tax, describing it as economically and ecologically misguided. In contrast, SPD parliamentary leader Matthias Miersch highlighted that coalition negotiations on the matter remain ongoing.

items.title: State Security Investigates Flag Incident at Berlin Reichstag
items.summary: A 22-year-old man climbed a nearly 30-meter flagpole in front of the Reichstag building in Berlin, lowered the German federal flag, and raised a Palestinian flag. Police detained the suspect, and the state security service has opened an investigation into the incident.

items.title: Struggling FDP Gathers for Digital Party Conference
items.summary: Facing deep political difficulties after multiple election defeats, the Free Democratic Party held a digital party conference to rally its ranks for upcoming state elections. Party leader Wolfgang Kubicki sought to position the liberals as an assertive counterweight to the federal government.

items.title: Minimal Special Federal Funds Released for Education
items.summary: According to media reports, only a fraction of the federal special funds earmarked for schools, daycare centers, and research has actually been invested in educational infrastructure. The slow disbursement of allocated funding has drawn sharp criticism from the Green Party.

items.title: Many German Properties Lack Natural Hazard Insurance
items.summary: Despite rising instances of costly damage from heavy rainfall and floods, only roughly half of all buildings in Germany are insured against severe weather hazards. Insurance and consumer experts warn of significant risks and demand decisive political action.

countries.overview: Turkey's current agenda is defined by high-stakes diplomacy, regional security transitions, and domestic regulatory scrutiny. President Erdoğan's visit to Baku resolved recent diplomatic friction with Azerbaijan, while the formal handover process of the Bashiqa base signals an evolving security posture with Iraq. As the UN COP31 summit in Antalya raises Turkey's international profile, the widening financial investigation into stock market funds and reports on expired pharmaceuticals highlight pressing governance and oversight challenges at home.

items.title: Erdoğan and Aliyev display unity following weeks of bilateral tension
items.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan met with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in Azerbaijan after weeks of heightened diplomatic tensions between Ankara and Baku. In a joint press briefing, both leaders reaffirmed their alliance against external efforts aimed at weakening their bilateral partnership.

items.title: Turkey and Iraq begin handover of Bashiqa military base
items.summary: Turkey and Iraq announced in a joint statement that the official process to transfer the Bashiqa military base to Iraqi security forces has commenced. The withdrawal of Turkish armed forces follows a bilateral security agreement reached in late September.

items.title: COP31 climate summit opens in Antalya under Turkish-Australian presidency
items.summary: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference has convened in Antalya, co-chaired by Turkey and Australia amid mounting international climate risks. While official proceedings focus on electrification targets and emission limits, civil society advocates have called on international delegations to raise domestic civil liberties concerns with Ankara.

items.title: Banking watchdog official arrested in widening Turkish fund probe
items.summary: A department head at Turkey's Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency (BDDK), Bilal Soysal, has been arrested in connection with the fund crisis that triggered severe losses on Borsa Istanbul. With this latest ruling, the total number of people arrested in the investigation has risen to 118.

items.title: Allegations of expired cancer drug resales spark health inspection debate
items.summary: Allegations that expired cancer treatments are being illicitly repackaged and resold on the Turkish market have prompted scrutiny of public pharmaceutical controls. Health experts are examining supervisory procedures and warning of severe, life-threatening risks to vulnerable patients.
